currentContext.business: The Company offers online matchmaking services on internet and mobile platforms, delivering them to users in India and the Indian diaspora through websites, mobile sites and mobile apps complemented by a wide on-the-ground network in India through marquee brands such as BharatMatrimony, CommunityMatrimony and EliteMatrimony. Revenue comprises membership subscription, service fees for personalised services and sales from online advertising packages, with subscription packages typically ranging from 3 months, 6 months and 1 year. The Company reports two business segments, Matchmaking and Marriage Services, and has expanded into wedding services (Mandap, Wedding Bazaar) and adjacent offerings such as MeraLuv.com, Luv.com, WeddingGiftBox, WedAssist, AstroChat and ManyJobs.

Governance of capital and controls sits with a Board of six directors of whom not less than 50% are independent, with a qualified and independent Audit Committee - all members Non-Executive and Independent Directors, chaired by an Independent Director - overseeing accounting and financial governance, and with board skills matrices explicitly covering strategy, finance (including oversight of funding arrangements, budgets and the efficient use of resources) and risk.|Governance of ESG is board-level: oversight of risk management sits with the Company's Risk Management and ESG Committee, which is responsible for identifying and mitigating risks and reports to the Board of Directors at the top of the corporate governance structure. Each mitigation plan is assigned to specific owners, set against defined timelines, and regularly monitored and reviewed.|Data privacy as the Company's principal ESG-material commitment: a comprehensive DPDP readiness programme covering consent management, privacy notices, vendor data processing agreements, grievance redressal mechanisms, data retention policies and appointment of a Data Protection Officer, with product workflows being re-engineered to embed 'privacy by design'.|Member-safety and trust controls: multi-factor authentication, ID and photo verification, AI-driven fraud detection and round-the-clock security monitoring, with regular employee security awareness training.|Gender diversity: women make up 55% of total employees (1,584 of 2,873, and 1,408 of 2,571 permanent employees), and 33.33% of the Board of Directors are women, of whom one is independent. The Company reports it has no 'workers' as defined in the BRSR guidance note.|Grievance redressal mechanisms are in place for shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with published web links or dedicated email IDs for each stakeholder group; no complaints were pending resolution at the close of the year for the categories disclosed.|CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013.|The BRSR is prepared on a standalone basis for Matrimony.com Limited only, and no external assurance provider has been appointed - assurance is reported as Not Applicable, which limits the verifiability of the ESG disclosures.
currentContext.expansion: Matrimony.com is an asset-light consumer-internet business, so expansion is expressed as retail footprint, experience centres, platform build-out and new verticals rather than plant capacity. The corporate overview cites a network of 120+ retail stores, and the MD&A names retail expansion, integration of vernacular languages and a focus on personalised services as the levers through which the Company differentiates. Capital expenditure during the year was modest relative to operating cash generation, and the Company remained debt-free at 31 March 2026 with a healthy liquid-asset position that management cites as backing for its expansion plans. For FY 2026-27, the stated expansion agenda is to set up additional Elite Matrimony Experience Centres, building on the success seen in initial markets; to scale WeddingGiftBox by first achieving the desired success rate for partners in South India and then rolling out in phases across India; and to establish Mandap and ManyJobs as successful propositions in Tamil Nadu before scaling to additional States. Alongside this, the Company continues to build out adjacent platforms - MeraLuv.com for Indian Americans, Luv.com for Next-Gen serious relationships, and WedAssist and AstroChat - and reports that ManyJobs gained meaningful momentum during the year, reaching one million registered job seekers and over 10,000 recruiters. In Wedding Services the model was recalibrated towards a commission-led approach with an initial focus on venue bookings, with product-market fit to be refined before scaling. The Company also made a strategic investment during the year in Bharat Ek Khoj Spiritual Tech Private Limited, an AI-powered platform for astrology-related services and for learning Vedic Shastra. Investment is also going into the technology platform itself - higher technology, professional consulting and infrastructure costs were incurred to support new initiatives - and into an AI-first operating model intended to optimise the workforce required across service and sales functions.
currentContext.mdna: Management expects growth momentum to improve as deferred revenues unwind and renewal cycles strengthen, with the calibrated investment approach supporting improving profitability over time|Longer-tenure subscription plans have strengthened the quality and visibility of future revenue streams; as these cohorts mature and renew they position the Company for improved growth momentum|Average Transaction Value grew 11.9% on premiumisation through Elite Matrimony, Assisted Services and longer-tenure plans, while paid subscription volumes moderated to 9.63 lakhs - the two key drivers of the matchmaking business are paid profiles and ATV|Implementation of longer-duration revenue plans caused revenue growth to lag billing growth (matchmaking billings grew 8.3% in FY26), a timing drag on reported revenue and margin|Margin drag came from higher employee costs and continued investment in new growth initiatives; other expenses rose on higher technology, professional consulting and infrastructure costs to support new initiatives|Marketing spend was held disciplined and marginally below the prior year to support brand visibility despite growth in newly launched initiatives|AI-led automation is expected to optimise the workforce required across both service and sales functions|Finance income depends on the investment corpus and treasury yields, which were lower on repo rate cuts by the RBI|Management positions the Company on market leadership in online matchmaking, a differentiated micro-market strategy, a healthy cash position, an AI-first approach and a strengthened leadership team to navigate the evolving consumer landscape in FY 2026-27 and beyond|Wedding services faced near-term challenges as the business model was recalibrated towards a commission-led approach with an initial focus on venue bookings|Not disclosed as an order book. The closest forward-visibility disclosure is deferred revenue from longer-tenure subscription plans: subscription billings are recognised as revenue over the subscription period (packages of 3, 6 and 12 months), and management states these plans 'have strengthened the quality and visibility of our future revenue streams' and expects growth momentum to improve as deferred revenues unwind and renewal cycles strengthen.

risks.risk: Business and market risk - shifting consumer preferences and attitudes toward arranged matrimony
risks.note: Changes in consumer preferences, particularly among younger, digitally-native users, and evolving attitudes toward arranged matrimony may impact subscription growth; regulations affecting digital platforms could influence profitability and expansion. The BRSR material-issues table flags the financial implication as negative - a slowdown in revenue. Mitigation is retail expansion, vernacular integration, a focus on personalised services and adjacent offerings (MeraLuv.com, Luv.com, Mandap.com, WeddingBazaar, AstroChat, WedAssist, ManyJobs), plus engagement in regulatory forums.

risks.risk: Competition risk from global dating apps, freemium regional players and vertical-specific platforms
risks.note: Competition can significantly affect the Company's market position, pricing and margins; the BRSR flags the implication as negative and able to lead to slower growth and profits. The Company defends leadership through continuous product innovation, a portfolio of 300+ community portals and 17 regional platforms, a network of 120+ retail outlets and brand recognition across BharatMatrimony and allied brands.

risks.risk: Data protection and privacy risk under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act
risks.note: Operationalisation of the DPDP Act imposes substantive obligations on entities handling personal data, and matrimonial information is unusually sensitive - community, religion, income and photographs - so non-compliance could result in regulatory action, financial penalties and reputational damage, along with legal costs and loss of customer trust. Mitigated through a DPDP readiness programme covering consent management, privacy notices, vendor data processing agreements, grievance redressal, data retention policies, appointment of a Data Protection Officer, and re-engineering of product workflows to embed 'privacy by design'.

risks.risk: Cybersecurity and technology-failure risk, including AI-generated fake profiles
risks.note: Technology failures, IT system breakdowns, cybersecurity breaches and threats such as phishing and social engineering could disrupt operations and harm reputation, while the growing incidence of AI-generated fake profiles and synthetic content poses new risks to member trust. Mitigated by periodic vulnerability assessments and internal audits, multi-factor authentication, ID and photo verification, AI-driven fraud detection, round-the-clock security monitoring and regular employee security awareness training.

risks.risk: Platform and regulatory dependence on third-party ecosystems
risks.note: A significant share of user acquisition and transactions flows through third-party ecosystems including app stores, search engines and digital advertising platforms, so changes in their policies, algorithms or commission structures could materially affect unit economics. Mitigated by diversifying acquisition channels across search, social, referrals and retail.

risks.risk: Revenue and activity concentration in a single business line
risks.note: The BRSR reports that 100% of turnover comes from one main activity - data processing, hosting and related activities, web portal - with matchmaking services alone contributing 99.05% of turnover and marriage services and related products only 0.95%. Business performance is therefore almost entirely dependent on the matchmaking subscription franchise and its two drivers, paid profiles and average transaction value, with paid profiles at 9.63 lakhs as of 31 March 2026 compared with 9.95 lakhs a year earlier.

risks.risk: Very high employee attrition concentrated in call-centre and entry-level roles
risks.note: The BRSR turnover-rate table shows a 96% total turnover rate for permanent employees in FY 2025-26 (94% in FY 2024-25 and 115% in FY 2023-24). The Company attributes this to high attrition in call-centre operations and related entry-level positions, which it states constitute 96% of its workforce; excluding those categories the FY26 turnover rate is 28%. Because service delivery is Relationship Manager and call-centre led, this churn is structural to the operating model.

risks.risk: Geographic concentration in India with a modest overseas contribution
risks.note: Operations are concentrated in India - 136 locations comprising the head office, 12 branch offices and 123 retail outlets, serving markets across Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Orissa, Delhi, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, West Bengal and Pondicherry - with exports at 11.79% of turnover, served through subsidiaries in the USA, Dubai and Bangladesh catering to NRI and Bangladeshi customers.

risks.risk: High volume of consumer complaints and consumer-forum exposure
risks.note: The BRSR grievance table records 1,10,666 customer complaints filed during FY 2025-26 (1,22,702 in FY 2024-25), which the Company attributes to improved visibility and tracking following integration of email correspondence into the ticket management system. A consumer-facing subscription model of this scale carries continuing consumer-redressal and reputational exposure.

one-line thesis: Matrimony.com delivered double-digit billing growth (10.5% YoY) driven by premiumization and a shift to longer-duration packages, though FY26 revenue stagnated (+0.9%) due to deferred recognition from these new packages. The core matchmaking business is showing operating leverage with expanding margins, while new verticals (Wedding, Jobs) remain loss-making experimental bets with no near-term breakeven expected.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 116.8 Cr (+7.9% YoY); EBITDA: INR 14.5 Cr (Margin 12.4% vs 10.8% YoY); PAT: INR 9.7 Cr (+18.9% YoY); Full Year PAT: INR 34.2 Cr (-24.5% YoY) due to lower finance income from buybacks/rate cuts and higher expenses; One-offs: INR 58.5 Cr share buyback in Q4; Accounting Distortion: INR 28 Cr gap between billing and revenue in FY26 due to deferral of 1-year 'Till You Marry' packs launched in March '25.
guidance: Q1FY27: Double-digit or high single-digit billing growth; Double-digit revenue growth; PAT to more than double vs Q1FY26; Marketing spend to remain flat at ~INR 45-46 Cr/quarter; No specific capex guidance but continued investment in new verticals.
order book & pipeline: N/A (Subscription model); Paid profiles at 2.34 lakhs (-4.3% YoY, +3.3% QoQ); Average Transaction Value (ATV) up 15.3% YoY.
segment / subsidiary detail: Matchmaking: Billing INR 125.4 Cr (+10.5% YoY), Revenue INR 116 Cr (+8.4% YoY), EBITDA margin 22% (up from 17.7% YoY). Marriage Services & Others: Billing INR 0.73 Cr (-40.7% YoY), EBITDA loss INR 5.7 Cr (widened from INR 3.2 Cr in Q3), includes ManyJobs and new Wedding Services model.
growth verticals / optionality: Elite Matrimony Centers (first store opened in Hyderabad); ManyJobs (1M users, 10k companies, monetization started in Tamil Nadu); Luv.com (serious matchmaking for metros); AI-based Astrology (experimental + stake in external startup).
margins & cost dynamics: Matchmaking EBITDA margin ex-marketing is stable at 59% (vs 58% Q3); Consolidated marketing spend reduced to INR 43.5 Cr in Q4 (vs INR 46.7 Cr YoY) due to optimization; Core margins expanding as 1-year package costs amortize over longer periods.
capex / expansion: Not explicitly quantified; Focus on strategic capex for physical Elite Centers and technology/AI integration; Opex focused on experimental verticals.
capital allocation: INR 58.5 Cr share buyback executed in Q4FY26; Cash & investments balance at INR 308 Cr; Management open to inorganic growth/acquisitions if opportunities arise; Continued funding of loss-making new ventures.
risks & watch-items: Persistent losses in Wedding/Other segments with no near-term breakeven; Decline in paid profile count (-4.3% YoY) despite billing growth; Dependence on marketing efficiency; Regulatory/Personal promoter pledge overhang (clarified as personal); Lower finance income due to rate cuts and cash deployment.
management quality / tone: Confident on core turnaround and operating leverage starting Q1FY27; Cautious/Experimental on new verticals (Wedding, Jobs, Astrology) admitting they are 'long way to go' for breakeven; Defensive on promoter shareholding queries.
non-obvious takeaways: The significant divergence between billing growth (+8% FY26) and revenue growth (+0.9% FY26) is purely mechanical due to the introduction of 1-year packages in March '25, creating a large deferred revenue bucket that will flip to P&L in FY27, artificially suppressing FY26 profits while boosting future visibility.

themes.title: Jewellery & wedding-economy formalization
themes.need: Organized jewellery is gaining share via capital-light FOCO expansion and GST/hallmarking formalization, even amid record gold-price volatility. KALYANKJIL posted Q4 revenue +66% YoY with 150 new FY27 stores and a near-zero non-GML-debt target; SENCO/PNGJL/DPABHUSHAN ride regional formalization; SKYGOLD/RGL/GOLDIAM on B2B and lab-grown export; KALAMANDIR on the wedding-wear economy.
themes.driver: Akshaya Tritiya / wedding-season demand; FOCO store rollout; gold-price stabilization lifting volumes.

themes.title: Digital platforms, SaaS, payments & cybersecurity
themes.need: Digital-public-infrastructure scale, enterprise SaaS and a compliance/security upcycle drive a distinct platform cohort. PINELABS/NPST/CMSINFO on payments; AURIONPRO/NEWGEN/NUCLEUS/ROUTE/TANLA on banking/CPaaS software; EMUDHRA/META(544441)/AURIONPRO on digital-identity & cybersecurity; CAPILLARY/MAPMYINDIA/NAZARA on SaaS/geospatial/gaming. Q1FY27 anchored the payments leg: PAYTM's GMV grew 31% YoY (accelerating 23% -> 27% -> 31%) with merchant payments about 80% of the financial-services mix and 25-30 lakh device additions a year on a distribution-only lending model (no book, no FLDG); MOBIKWIK posted payments GMV of INR 52,400cr (+58% YoY), a 13th consecutive record quarter and India's largest wallet by GTV at ~20% share, against only ~INR 3,200cr of digital-credit GMV. OFSS adds the banking-software annuity, with RPO +17% YoY versus revenue +7% and licence-and-cloud revenue +13% at a 44% operating margin.
themes.driver: Deal/ARR additions; festive digital-payments TPV; merchant-device additions; RBI/regulatory compliance-driven security spend.

hero.oneLiner: Matrimony.com Limited is India's #1 online matchmaking company, running a portfolio of matrimony, community and premium matchmaking platforms backed by a retail network and Relationship Manager-led assisted services, and is expanding into adjacent wedding, dating and allied services.
